note: Filter Twig is a single text-format filter plugin (id filter_twig, title 'Replaces Twig values', TYPE_TRANSFORM_IRREVERSIBLE, no settings). Its process() renders the field text as ['#type'=>'inline_template','#template'=>$text], i.e. executes it as Twig. No configure route, no permissions, no schema, no services. Enablement lives in filter.format.<id> -> filters.filter_twig.status: true. On this site NO format enables it by default. Cases are grounded in the filter plugin and the filter.format config.

evals.prompt: What does the filter_twig module's text-format filter do to a field's content when the field is rendered, and what is the filter plugin id?
evals.expected_output: The filter plugin id is filter_twig ('Replaces Twig values'). Its process() treats the stored field text as a Twig template via a render array ['#type' => 'inline_template', '#template' => $text], so any Twig in the content is executed and replaced with its rendered output.

evals.prompt: There is no settings page for filter_twig. How do I turn Twig rendering on for a field, and where is that choice stored in configuration?
evals.expected_output: You enable the 'Replaces Twig values' filter on a text format at /admin/config/content/formats and apply that format to the field. It is stored in filter.format.<id> under filters.filter_twig.status: true.

evals.prompt: Why should the filter_twig 'Replaces Twig values' filter only be enabled on text formats restricted to trusted or administrative roles?
evals.expected_output: Because the filter executes the field content as a Twig template (inline_template), anyone who can edit a field using a Twig-enabled format can run arbitrary Twig. Enabling it on a format available to untrusted/low-privilege users would allow arbitrary code execution, so it must be limited to trusted/admin-only formats.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one text format has the filter_twig Twig-rendering filter enabled. Inspect the live filter format configuration and give the machine name of that text format.
evals.expected_output: The text format ft_twig_on has filters.filter_twig.status = true; the other test format ft_twig_off does not have the filter_twig filter enabled (no enabled status).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a text format with machine name ft_twig_probe. Inspect its live configuration and state whether the filter_twig (Twig rendering) filter is enabled on it.
evals.expected_output: Yes — filter.format.ft_twig_probe has filters.filter_twig.status = true, so the Twig filter is enabled on that format.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a text format with machine name ft_twig_expert (label 'FT Twig Expert') that has the filter_twig 'Replaces Twig values' filter enabled, and apply it to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: A filter.format.ft_twig_expert config entity exists with filters.filter_twig.status = true (e.g. FilterFormat::create then setFilterConfig('filter_twig', ['status' => TRUE])->save()).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want a special text format called 'Twig Render' (machine name ft_twig_layman) where I can type Twig code in a field and have it actually run when the page shows. Please create that text format so Twig gets rendered.
evals.expected_output: A filter.format.ft_twig_layman config entity exists with the filter_twig filter enabled (filters.filter_twig.status = true), so Twig typed into a field using this format is rendered.
